signal: Many range-sum (or range-count) queries on an array that does not change
why: Precompute P[i] = a[0] + ... + a[i-1] once; any range sum is P[r+1] - P[l], so each query is O(1) instead of O(n).

signal: Many 'add x to every element in [l, r]' updates, with the final array needed only after all updates
why: Record +x at l and -x at r+1 in O(1) per update, then one prefix-sum pass rebuilds the final array.

signal: Sorted array (or one you may sort) and you must find or count pairs satisfying a sum or difference condition
why: When moving a pointer can only help (or only hurt) the condition, each pointer sweeps the array once, replacing a nested loop.
constraints: n up to 2*10^5; brute force pairs is O(n^2)

signal: Longest, shortest or number of subarrays where a property survives shrinking the window (for example non-negative sums, at most k distinct values)
why: Validity is monotone: if a window is valid, every sub-window is valid. So the left end only moves right and the whole scan is amortised linear.

signal: Maximum (or minimum) sum of a contiguous subarray, values may be negative
why: The best subarray ending at i either extends the best ending at i-1 or starts fresh at i, so one running value suffices.

signal: Sorted data and a question like 'first position with value >= x' or 'how many elements are <= x'
why: The predicate flips from false to true exactly once along the order, so halving the range finds the flip point.

signal: 'Minimise the maximum' or 'maximise the minimum', or the answer is a number and checking 'is value v achievable?' is easy and monotone in v
why: If v is feasible then every larger (or smaller) v is too, so search the value range with a greedy or simulated feasibility check.
constraints: answer up to 10^9 or 10^18; check must be about O(n)

signal: Maximise or minimise a function that strictly rises then falls (unimodal) over a continuous or integer range
why: Comparing two interior points tells you which outer third cannot contain the optimum, so each step discards a third of the range.
constraints: a flat plateau away from the optimum breaks it

signal: Intervals, meetings, events or points where only the relative order of starts/ends matters
why: After sorting by a key, conflicts or overlaps only need to be checked against the neighbouring or currently open items.

signal: Values go up to 10^9 or 10^18 but there are only n of them, and you want array indexing or a Fenwick/segment tree over values
why: Replace each value by its rank among the sorted distinct values; relative order is preserved and indices shrink to at most n.
constraints: n up to 2*10^5, values up to 10^9
